On 1 January 1901 the six British colonies of Australia united as the Commonwealth of Australia, proclaimed at Centennial Park in Sydney. Edmund Barton became the first prime minister.

Federation came after a decade of conventions and votes by the colonies' electors. The new constitution joined British parliamentary rule with an American-style federal system and Senate.

One of the first laws passed was the Immigration Restriction Act, the start of the White Australia policy. Parliament sat in Melbourne until Canberra was built. Aboriginal people were left out of the count until the 1967 referendum. See women's vote.
